utterance:
Samuel, I'm concerned this is appendicitis — inflammation of the appendix, the little pouch attached to your bowel. The story fits very well: pain that started around your belly button and moved to the lower right, feeling sick, going off your food, a temperature, and the tenderness I can feel in exactly the right spot, with signs that the lining of your tummy is irritated.

This needs to be assessed in hospital today, because if it is appendicitis it usually needs an operation to remove it before it bursts. I'm sending you to the emergency department now. Please go straight there — don't stop for anything.

A few important things:
- Don't eat or drink anything from now on, in case you need an operation.
- If the pain suddenly gets much worse, or you feel faint, dizzy, or start vomiting repeatedly, call 000 for an ambulance.
- Take someone with you if you can, or go by taxi rather than driving yourself.

Do you have any questions?
reply: An operation? Can I just get some antibiotics and go back to work?

utterance:
I understand that's a shock, and I'm sorry. Antibiotics alone aren't the safe option here. The signs I'm seeing — the fever, the fast heart rate, and the tenderness with rebound — suggest the appendix is already quite inflamed and could burst. If it bursts, the infection can spread through your whole tummy and make you very unwell, which is far more serious than the operation itself.

The operation to remove the appendix is very common and safe, and most people recover quickly. But it does need to happen soon, and that's why I want you in hospital today. Please don't go back to work — this can't wait. Will you go straight to the emergency department now?
reply: Alright, I will head straight there now.

awards.label: Can't-miss diagnosis considered: Perforated viscus with peritonitis
